note: Severe bleeding risk: Synergistic anticoagulant and antiplatelet effect dramatically elevates major GI and intracranial hemorrhage risk.
Lactic acidosis risk: Metformin combined with iodinated radiocontrast agents can precipitate acute renal impairment and fatal lactic acidosis.
Hyperkalemia risk: ARB plus potassium-sparing diuretic significantly elevates serum potassium; requires renal and electrolyte monitoring.
Rhabdomyolysis risk: CYP3A4 inhibition increases statin systemic exposure, increasing risk of severe myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Hypoglycemia risk: Salicylates displace sulfonylureas from protein binding sites, increasing free drug and risk of profound hypoglycemia.
Hepatotoxicity risk: Duplicate paracetamol intake exceeds maximum 4000mg/day threshold, risking acute liver injury.
